question.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{coth}⁡x$ and $v(x)={e}^{x}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot {e}^{x}-\operatorname{coth}⁡x\cdot {({e}^{x})}^{′}}{{({e}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-{csch}^{2}⁡x)\cdot {e}^{x}-\operatorname{coth}⁡x\cdot ({e}^{x})}{{e}^{2x}} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{x}({csch}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{coth}⁡x)}{{e}^{2x}} \\  & =-\frac{{csch}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{coth}⁡x}{{e}^{x}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
